1KI 7:38-50.appendix: \ip 7. \it Verse\it* 1, etc. See the first 12 verses of this chapter placed at the end of it in the Vatican copy.
1KI 7:38-50.why: Print the chapter in the order of Alexandrinus, confirmed by Swete (vol. I, p. 687: VII 38–50 anteponit A): Solomon’s house, Brenton’s 7:38–50, before the works of Chiram, as the Hebrew orders them. Brenton’s printings number the chapter by the King James numbers, so his Appendix calls them the first 12 verses; eBible’s numbers are Swete’s, and the verses keep them. A also words both ends otherwise, as the Hebrew does: at 38 it adds that he finished all his house (p. 690: ετη] αιτεσιν· και συνετελεσεν ολον τον οικον αυτου· A), and at 50 it has instead the court of the porch, which it leaves out at 6:36–36a (p. 687: om κυκλοθεν...ναου A; p. 691: 50 συνετελεσεν… αυτου] οικοδομησε αυλην οικου κ̅υ̅ την εσωτατην των αιλαμ του οικου του κατα προσωπον του ναου· A); Brenton reports neither, so the verses keep his words. Brenton printed only See Appendix at 7:1 (1879 p. 468; 1844 vol. 1 p. 394), restored by a correction and taken up here; the edition’s notes stand at each place, as the New Testament’s moved verses are noted. The Appendix paragraph is identical in 1879 printed p. 1133 (physical 1149) and 1900 printed p. 1133 (physical 1145): “7. Verse 1, etc. See the first 12 verses of this chapter placed at the end of it in the Vatican copy.” These are Brenton’s Hebrew-numbered verses, represented by eBible’s 7:38–50, including its separate closing clause at 50; the move changes order, not the wording or source numbering.

1KI 14:1-20.appendix: \ip 14. \it Verses\it* 1 to 20. The substance of these verses is found in the Vatican copy after \it v\it*. 24, \it chap\it*. 12.

Irregular constructions are explained explicitly; unresolved each and with at 14:8 remain in the note rather than receiving a conjectural translation. At 14:15 retain the KJV beyond the river for απο περαν του ποταμου: the scattering is beyond the river, and Brenton likewise renders απο του περαν του Ιορδανου locatively as on the other side of Jordan at Joshua 14:2, rather than requiring English from. The separate omission follows Swete p. 708: A lacks all of 12:24a–z, so both accounts must not stand in the main text. Brenton’s source notes and Appendix notice remain exactly pinned. Names are revised by their bearers at the revise stage. The Hebrew of 14:14–17 is checked against the Masoretic text (https://mechon-mamre.org/p/pt/pt09a14.htm): that day, beyond the river, and threshold of the door are identified as KJV renderings, not falsely attributed as different Hebrew words.

EZK 1:14.why: Supply Ezekiel 1:14 before 1:15 from the Authorized Version, which renders the Hebrew verse Brenton reports; A’s βεζεκ transliterates the Hebrew word that the Authorized Version renders a flash of lightning. Brenton 1879 physical p. 996 and 1900 physical p. 992 (printed p. 980) place θ after lightning. at the end of 1:13, immediately before 1:15, and print “Alex. and Heb. supply ver. 14. ‘And the living creatures ran and returned at the appearance of Bezec.’” Brenton 1844 vol. II physical p. 304 (printed p. 801) gives the same sentence in a marginal note called by a dagger after “lightning.” The 1884 physical p. 955 preserves the body and its θ caller, but its footnote band is cropped away and cannot independently confirm the note. CCEL 15#6 misreads the final c as e; the build sets its closing caller at the end of 1:13, as printed, under the key EZK 1:13 CCEL#2. In Swete III p. 386, checked against the scan, B’s main text passes directly from 1:13 to 1:15; explicit apparatus adds και τα ζωα ετρεχον και ανεκαμπτον ως ειδος του βεζεκ A et (sub θʹ ✣) Q. A is unqualified, without correcting hand, lacuna, or uncertainty; Q has a Theodotion source marker, not an A hand. Brenton’s Bezec transliterates βεζεκ, the Hebrew lightning word; his at does not express the Greek comparison ως. Pinned KJV Ezekiel 1:14 supplies the complete matching sentence “And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.” The pinned RV1885 has the identical sentence. Retain the complete KJV sentence under the house-style provision for passages whose English Brenton left incomplete; the introduction explains this case. Copy the entire KJV verse instead of splicing syntax or inventing a translation. B positively omits the verse independently of Brenton’s facing Greek, which also omits it.

NUM 28:24.why: Keep seven days in the text and two days in the footnote. Brenton 1879 (physical page 232, printed page 216) and 1900 (physical page 228, printed page 216) both put the caller before seven days and print “Alex. two days.” Swete I, p. 319 confirms δυο sup ras A^a, the corrector’s two over an erasure. Treat it as a scribal slip within the feast sequence: the base text specifies seven days of unleavened bread at 28:17 and a holy convocation on the seventh day at 28:25. A omits the seven-day clause at 28:17, so that clause is not evidence of A contradicting itself; the seventh-day close at 28:25 still frames this daily feast offering. The erasure alone is not grounds for rejection, since corrected readings are printed elsewhere (PSA 91:10).
